Look at the yield from the shares, not the price.
The big 4 banks have a wide range of prices but their yield is similar. So, $1000 worth of CBA will yield you the same return as $1000 worth of ANZ, for example…. But the number of shares you hold will be different.

Not sure who the AC/DC you’re talking about is. The ACDC ETF is currently trading at about $101 a share.
Use a brokerage that doesn't charge per trade to start with.

Retired from investment properties capital etf for an afterthought

I retired at 57 and have been living off dividends for a while now. 

I invest using a strategy not discussed here.  I invest for ‘dividend growth’, in that I look for companies that not only have a long history of not only paying a dividend, but also a long history of increasing the dividend every year. 

Since 2020 my dividend income has increased almost 40%. 

The ‘expert’ here wasn’t much of an expert, in my opinion.  

This works if you do it right and you can do it in a lot less than 30 years. 

I’m Canadian and invest in that market.  We have good dividend growers that pay sustainable, growing dividends from less than 1% up to 7%.  It just depends on the amount of capital growth you want. 

My portfolio currently pays about a ~3.8% yield right now and it grows every year about 4-5%.

You should attempt to talk to people that are actually there and have real world experience.

I’m not a professional, just a guy that had to build his own ‘pension’.
